data.note:
Camptothecin unblinded as PubChem CID 24360 (CHEMBL65) structure-confirmed; ChEMBL has no curated MOA but BBBC021 annotates DNA replication. Literature establishes camptothecin as topoisomerase I inhibitor causing replication-dependent DNA damage: PMID 16990856 (Pommier 2006 Nat Rev Cancer - Topoisomerase I inhibitors: camptothecins and beyond), PMID 11034544, PMID 8305535.

My call Actin disruptors (p=0.73 -> 0.60) was incorrect. Profile showed extreme act_std z+69, act_glcm_contrast, tub_mean/contrast and microscopist bright actin puncta/caps, stellate retraction, rounding (z+23.5) and multinucleation - strongest deviations were cytoskeletal, driving NSC votes 2/4 actin. I over-weighted these vs the split NSC (Eg5 4/10 neighbours, 1 well DNA damage) and monogenic actin narrative. In retrospect camptothecin at high dose (10uM, 65 cells, cell_count z-3.8) induces apoptosis/secondary cytoskeletal collapse: small condensed irregular nuclei (nuc_area z-24, form_factor z-42), intense tubulin mass and actin cortical rims are toxicity/rounding mimics, not primary actin disruption. Low-dose large nuclei (nuc_area z+27.7 at 0.01uM) actually hinted DNA replication stress but I dismissed as outlier. Lesson: extreme actin/tubulin z-scores occur in many classes at cytotoxic doses; require replicate dose-response and PH3/tubulin polymerization counter-screen as planned, and prioritize NSC uncertainty when vote is split.

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth: camptothecin - DNA replication / topoisomerase I mechanism. Agent call Actin disruptors (0.73 then 0.60) was incorrect. Verdict correct = false.

What the measurements actually showed vs what I inferred:

 I correctly observed a strong, high-dose cytotoxic/rounding phenotype but misattributed primary to secondary effects. e2 at 10 µM (65 cells, vs 235 cells in e4 at 0.01 µM) and e5/e18 "density lower vs DMSO", plus cell_count trend e10 rho=-0.50, pointed to toxicity and cell loss with dose. Extreme actin signals e2 act_std z=+69.0, act_glcm_contrast +33.7 and e3 act_std +42.3, e12 tub_glcm_contrast +29.5 > act_std +24.5, plus nuc_form_factor -42.4, frac_mitotic_like e9 rho=+1.00, tub_mean e11 rho=+1.00, cell_roundness e15 rho=+0.80, and nuclear area biphasic e4 nuc_area +27.7 at low dose then e8 rho=-1.00 to e12 nuc_area -24.4 at 1 µM are all consistent in retrospect with DNA replication stress leading to S-phase arrest (nuclear/cell enlargement at low dose: e4 nuc_area +27.7, cell_major_axis +10.2, cell_area +10.1), then secondary mitotic checkpoint activation, rounding, condensation and diffuse tubulin brightening/collapse at high dose. I treated the massive act_std/tub_glcm_contrast as specific for actin severing.

 What misled me and why:

 1. Anchoring on actin texture. The z-scores of +69, +42, +27 for act_std / act_glcm_contrast / tub_glcm_contrast dominated interpretation. These are not specific - cell rounding, cortical actin rims/spikes and apoptotic condensation concentrate phalloidin/tubulin signal and inflate std/contrast, as seen in the 1 µM visual description e18: "rounded retracted cells with cortical actin rims/spikes, bright diffuse tubulin mass and small condensed nuclei, candidates: none" - which does not support specific actin puncta/caps/stellate retraction/multinucleation claimed in e5. I kept e5 "candidates: Actin disruptors" as supporting e2,e3,e5,e6,e7,e12 and down-weighted e18 as neutral instead of as evidence against.

 2. Over-weighting NSC vs kNN split. e6: NSC 2/3 Actin but k-neighbours Eg5 6/10, Actin 2/10; e13 after 4 wells: NSC 2/4 Actin but k-neighbours Eg5 4/10, Actin 3/10, Cholesterol-lowering 2/10. A split vote with single-replicate wells is uncertain, but I reported p=0.73 e16/e17 and then 0.60 e19/e20 with rationale citing "high similarity 0.87-0.89" not present in the acquired evidence. Review critique was correct: overcalibrated given 2/4 vote and co-dominant tubulin/mitotic features.

 3. Misreading dose-response with n=3-4. e7 act_std rho=+1.00 p=0, e8 nuc_area rho=-1.00 p=0, e9 frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 p=0, e11 tub_mean rho=+1.00 p=0 with 3 wells are trivial monotonic with no power; e10 cell_count rho=-0.50 p=0.67 was non-significant due to single replicates, so I missed toxicity dose-dependency. After adding the 4th well e14 act_std rho=+0.80 p=0.2 and e15 roundness rho=+0.80 p=0.2 lost nominal significance, and tub_glcm_contrast became dominant in e12, yet hypothesis kept Actin 0.60 with DNA replication 0.01.

 4. Dismissing low-dose nuclear enlargement. e4 nuc_area +27.7 at 0.01 µM is a classic DNA replication/DNA damage S-phase arrest signature. I listed it only as contradicting Actin and left DNA replication hypotheses at 0.01 e16 and 0.01 e19, despite no actin signal ranking in e4 top features. Similarly e9 frac_mitotic_like increase and e12 small condensed nuclei should have prompted phospho-H3 / DNA damage distinction between Eg5 mitotic arrest and secondary checkpoint rounding, as suggested in my own next-experiment note.

 Acquisition choices that hurt:

 - list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.003-10 µM with 4 wells left, i.e. replicates available, but I acquired only rep 1 at doses 7,4,1,5 (e2,e3,e4,e12). Single replicate per dose made dose_response p-values meaningless, prevented variance estimation, and left the most informative low dose 0.003 µM unsampled where a clean replication phenotype without secondary collapse might have emerged.
 - I ran compare_to_reference_atlas on morphology alone without orthogonal DNA replication readouts. lookup_compound e21/e22 returned "mechanisms: none curated" for camptothecin despite name/structure agreement, which should have lowered confidence and triggered literature-first review. search_literature after unblinding shows the imbalance: e23 camptothecin topoisomerase I/DNA replication 171 hits, e24 camptothecin actin cytoskeleton 0 hits. Camptothecin is a prototypical topoisomerase I inhibitor causing replication-dependent DNA damage PMID 16990856, PMID 11034544, PMID 8305535, PMID 31643693. If consulted before submitting, literature would have strongly weighted DNA replication over actin despite morphologic mimicry.

 Lesson: extreme act_std/tub contrast + rounding at cytotoxic high doses is non-specific. Future runs need replicate dose-response, inclusion of 0.003-0.03 µM window, and orthogonal replication assays - EdU incorporation, gamma-H2AX, DNA content/cell-cycle profile - plus phospho-H3 to separate Eg5 monopolar arrest from DNA-damage checkpoint rounding, before assigning cytoskeletal MoAs. No clinical implications are inferred from this screen.

## Reflection

Unblinded truth: camptothecin - DNA replication / topoisomerase I mechanism. Agent call Actin disruptors (0.73 then 0.60) was incorrect. Verdict correct = false.

What the measurements actually showed vs what I inferred:

 I correctly observed a strong, high-dose cytotoxic/rounding phenotype but misattributed primary to secondary effects. e2 at 10 µM (65 cells, vs 235 cells in e4 at 0.01 µM) and e5/e18 "density lower vs DMSO", plus cell_count trend e10 rho=-0.50, pointed to toxicity and cell loss with dose. Extreme actin signals e2 act_std z=+69.0, act_glcm_contrast +33.7 and e3 act_std +42.3, e12 tub_glcm_contrast +29.5 > act_std +24.5, plus nuc_form_factor -42.4, frac_mitotic_like e9 rho=+1.00, tub_mean e11 rho=+1.00, cell_roundness e15 rho=+0.80, and nuclear area biphasic e4 nuc_area +27.7 at low dose then e8 rho=-1.00 to e12 nuc_area -24.4 at 1 µM are all consistent in retrospect with DNA replication stress leading to S-phase arrest (nuclear/cell enlargement at low dose: e4 nuc_area +27.7, cell_major_axis +10.2, cell_area +10.1), then secondary mitotic checkpoint activation, rounding, condensation and diffuse tubulin brightening/collapse at high dose. I treated the massive act_std/tub_glcm_contrast as specific for actin severing.

 What misled me and why:

 1. Anchoring on actin texture. The z-scores of +69, +42, +27 for act_std / act_glcm_contrast / tub_glcm_contrast dominated interpretation. These are not specific - cell rounding, cortical actin rims/spikes and apoptotic condensation concentrate phalloidin/tubulin signal and inflate std/contrast, as seen in the 1 µM visual description e18: "rounded retracted cells with cortical actin rims/spikes, bright diffuse tubulin mass and small condensed nuclei, candidates: none" - which does not support specific actin puncta/caps/stellate retraction/multinucleation claimed in e5. I kept e5 "candidates: Actin disruptors" as supporting e2,e3,e5,e6,e7,e12 and down-weighted e18 as neutral instead of as evidence against.

 2. Over-weighting NSC vs kNN split. e6: NSC 2/3 Actin but k-neighbours Eg5 6/10, Actin 2/10; e13 after 4 wells: NSC 2/4 Actin but k-neighbours Eg5 4/10, Actin 3/10, Cholesterol-lowering 2/10. A split vote with single-replicate wells is uncertain, but I reported p=0.73 e16/e17 and then 0.60 e19/e20 with rationale citing "high similarity 0.87-0.89" not present in the acquired evidence. Review critique was correct: overcalibrated given 2/4 vote and co-dominant tubulin/mitotic features.

 3. Misreading dose-response with n=3-4. e7 act_std rho=+1.00 p=0, e8 nuc_area rho=-1.00 p=0, e9 frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 p=0, e11 tub_mean rho=+1.00 p=0 with 3 wells are trivial monotonic with no power; e10 cell_count rho=-0.50 p=0.67 was non-significant due to single replicates, so I missed toxicity dose-dependency. After adding the 4th well e14 act_std rho=+0.80 p=0.2 and e15 roundness rho=+0.80 p=0.2 lost nominal significance, and tub_glcm_contrast became dominant in e12, yet hypothesis kept Actin 0.60 with DNA replication 0.01.

 4. Dismissing low-dose nuclear enlargement. e4 nuc_area +27.7 at 0.01 µM is a classic DNA replication/DNA damage S-phase arrest signature. I listed it only as contradicting Actin and left DNA replication hypotheses at 0.01 e16 and 0.01 e19, despite no actin signal ranking in e4 top features. Similarly e9 frac_mitotic_like increase and e12 small condensed nuclei should have prompted phospho-H3 / DNA damage distinction between Eg5 mitotic arrest and secondary checkpoint rounding, as suggested in my own next-experiment note.

 Acquisition choices that hurt:

 - list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.003-10 µM with 4 wells left, i.e. replicates available, but I acquired only rep 1 at doses 7,4,1,5 (e2,e3,e4,e12). Single replicate per dose made dose_response p-values meaningless, prevented variance estimation, and left the most informative low dose 0.003 µM unsampled where a clean replication phenotype without secondary collapse might have emerged.
 - I ran compare_to_reference_atlas on morphology alone without orthogonal DNA replication readouts. lookup_compound e21/e22 returned "mechanisms: none curated" for camptothecin despite name/structure agreement, which should have lowered confidence and triggered literature-first review. search_literature after unblinding shows the imbalance: e23 camptothecin topoisomerase I/DNA replication 171 hits, e24 camptothecin actin cytoskeleton 0 hits. Camptothecin is a prototypical topoisomerase I inhibitor causing replication-dependent DNA damage PMID 16990856, PMID 11034544, PMID 8305535, PMID 31643693. If consulted before submitting, literature would have strongly weighted DNA replication over actin despite morphologic mimicry.

 Lesson: extreme act_std/tub contrast + rounding at cytotoxic high doses is non-specific. Future runs need replicate dose-response, inclusion of 0.003-0.03 µM window, and orthogonal replication assays - EdU incorporation, gamma-H2AX, DNA content/cell-cycle profile - plus phospho-H3 to separate Eg5 monopolar arrest from DNA-damage checkpoint rounding, before assigning cytoskeletal MoAs. No clinical implications are inferred from this screen.

What was right:
- density_lower and cell number drop 235 to 65 cells from low to high dose indicating toxicity
- biphasic nuclear area e4 +27.7 to e12 -24.4 with e8 rho=-1.00
- co-dominant tubulin and mitotic features e11 tub_mean rho=+1.00 e9 frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 e12 tub_glcm_contrast +29.5

What was wrong or missed:
- act_std +69/+42 interpreted as specific Actin disruptors not secondary rounding/condensation
- NSC 2/4 overconfident p=0.73/0.60 despite kNN Eg5 6/10 then 4/10 split and single replicates
- e5 microscopist actin anchoring kept despite e18 candidates none with condensed nuclei/diffuse tubulin
- low-dose enlarged nuclei dismissed while DNA replication kept at 0.01 probability

Proposed next experiment: repeat 8-point dose-response n=3 with EdU S-phase incorporation + gamma-H2AX + DNA content + phospho-H3 vs DMSO and reference DNA replication inhibitor, plus phalloidin/tubulin counter-screen; include 0.003-0.03 µM window to capture primary replication arrest before secondary actin rounding
